title: Parents as a door
hook: the parent is the middle door of the garden (Tirmidhi)
tomorrow: an old photo: dad and a brother he never mentions. what happened?

segments.voice: Yesterday, mercy at home: a sandal mended, a grandson kissed, service at the sink. Today, the person in the house the tradition calls a door.

Nine at night, and two plans collide. A parent's knee exercises need someone to count the reps, slowly. A group chat says the study session is starting. Small choice. Hardly worth a thought. A hadith in Jami' at-Tirmidhi calls it something bigger: a door. The parent, it says, is the middle door of the garden of Paradise. Keep that door, or lose it. The word there is al-walid, the parent who gave you life.
screen: `TWO PLANS, ONE EVENING.` → `THE MIDDLE DOOR OF THE GARDEN.` → `KEEP IT, OR LOSE IT.`

segments.voice: Why the middle door? Some readers say it's the best one, and the closest. You don't cross a desert to reach it. It's down the hall. The Qur'an sets the tone for that hallway. In Pickthall's words: "lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy." A bird lowering its wing over its young, turned around: now the grown child shelters the parent. And it gives words to say with it: "My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little." Then a scene. A man came to the Prophet ﷺ asking permission to go and fight. The Prophet asked him: are your parents alive? Yes. Then strive in their service. The great effort he went looking for was waiting at home. Another man asked who most deserved his good company. Your mother, the Prophet said. Then who? Your mother. Then who? Your mother. Then who? Your father. So the door swings on two hinges. None of this asks anyone to stop living their own life. It asks what happens when two plans collide on a weeknight. One for tonight: the man looking for the hardest striving was sent home to his parents.
screen: `THE CLOSEST DOOR.` · `LOWER THE WING OF MERCY.` · `STRIVE IN THEIR SERVICE.` · `YOUR MOTHER, THREE TIMES.` · then, large: `THE MIDDLE DOOR.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers the things a parent, or whoever raised you or looked out for you, did when you were small that you couldn't do for yourself. Meals, rides, nights up with a fever, a hand on the way to school. If that relationship is hard, or they're gone, count what you honestly can. Some Muslims close with the Qur'an's words: my Lord, have mercy on them both.
screen: `WHAT THEY DID WHEN YOU WERE SMALL.` · `COUNT WHAT YOU HONESTLY CAN.`

segments.voice: Parents as a door: in the hadith, a parent is the middle door of the garden. Close by, and easy to walk past.
Your line: the middle door, just down the hall and open tonight. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1713 COUNTS.` → `FAMILY AND FRIENDSHIP · 2 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: AN OLD PHOTO. WHY DON'T THEY TALK?`

howItsDone: Muslims call honoring parents birr al-walidayn, and say the Qur'an's prayer from 17:24, 'my Lord, have mercy on them both', for parents living or gone.

fork.setup: your mom calls during your game, for the third time today, with the same question about her phone. what fits 'lower the wing'?
options: let it ring; you've already explained it twice today.
answer kindly and walk her through it again.
answer, but tell her this is the last time.
fork.reveal: the verse turns the bird's wing around: now the child shelters the parent, patiently, the way they once did for you.

original.note: Arabic: devotion to parents; the phrase Muslims use for honoring and serving them.

trapdoor: what you thought: honoring parents means doing whatever they say.
what it means: it means serving them up close, the way they once sheltered you.
what a scholar hears: Tirmidhi 1900 calls the parent the middle of the gates of Paradise; Bukhari 3004 sends a would-be fighter home: strive in their service.
guess: serving your parents as a way to God's garden
a doorway in the house kept for the eldest
obeying parents in every single thing they ask

chat.says: dad's knee reps need counting at 9. study group's at 9. he says 'go, i'm fine.' is he?
options: Count his reps, then join late. He's the middle door, even when he waves you off.
Go. He said he's fine, and honoring a parent means taking his word for it.
Skip both and pay for a trainer. Serving parents means paying for their help.
chat.meaning: The Prophet sent a man looking for a great effort home: strive in your parents' service. A parent is the middle door.

al-walid.meaning: the parent who gave you life; in Arabic, usually the father

Paradise.meaning: the garden of the life to come, in the Qur'an's picture

sources.ref: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1900 (Abu al-Darda': the parent is the middle of the gates of Paradise; keep that gate or lose it)

notes: Confirm the exact Pickthall wording of 17:24 (quoted in two parts in the teach).

Tirmidhi 1900: the word is al-walid (usually 'the father'); the outline says 'the parent'. The voice names the word and pairs it with Bukhari 5971 (the mother three times). 'Some readers say it's the best one, and the closest' is a hedge for the commentators' reading of 'middle' (awsat) as best; confirm.
Bukhari 3004 and 5971: confirm numbering and paraphrases.
The practice allows for hard or broken relationships with parents and for parents who have died.
